summary: Aroostook County, ME lookout on SR 163 east of Ashland: 1915 camp for the lookout man, 1916 repair; register says no longer standing, removal date not found.

facts.status_note: Register says the tower is no longer standing; no removal date found

events.note: New camp built for the lookout man on Haystack Mountain. Staffing inferred from the camp; no watchman is named

Lookout station repaired. In a letter dated November 15, 1916, the chief fire warden wrote that a new lookout ought to be built the next year; the Forest Lookouts page attributes the letter to the Daily Kennebec Journal
Registered September 15, 2008; nominated by Bob Spear

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives the Site I location as 671 ft (205 m). The Maine Memory postcard says Haystack Mountain is 1,142 feet high. The story uses the register figure for the site and reports the postcard figure only as the mountain's height.

notes_for_editor: Location is not settled. The Site I register entry puts the tower on SR 163 east of Ashland; the Maine Memory postcard and the Site II entry put Haystack Mountain at Castle Hill. The story reports both and does not reconcile them. The brief's FFLA point (46.66695, -68.23208) is about 2.7 km from the Site I register point and carries the same register number, US 76; check whether that point belongs to Site II. The brief says log construction (from FFLA); no fetched source confirms it. A search snippet from an FFLA Maine chapter Facebook post mentions a 1914 log lookout at Castle Hill; it was not fetched and is not cited. No construction date was found, so there is no built event. No access or visit information was found. Staffed 1915 is inferred from the camp for the lookout man.
